text:
marta: Heads-up — main is red after I regenerated poetry.lock on release/2026-q1. Windows wheel job is failing on cryptography native build. CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/217

ci-bot: Build #217 failed on windows-latest (wheel). Summary: failed wheel build for cryptography, job log attached.

marta: Excerpt from the log:
```
Building wheel for cryptography (pyproject.toml) ... error
ERROR: Failed building wheel for cryptography
error: Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 is required.
note: This usually means a binary wheel isn't available for this platform/version.
```

jonathan: Did the lock regen change the cryptography version or platform markers?

marta: I ran `poetry lock --no-update` locally on macOS and pushed the lockfile. The cryptography entry moved from 40.0.1 -> 40.1.0 in the lockfile (transitive from cffi update). No explicit platform markers.

emily: Can someone bisect the lockfile commit range? If this is a transitive bump, we should find the exact package that pulled it. I can take it if someone assigns the range.

rajesh: Quick triage: pinning cryptography back to 40.0.1 in pyproject.toml (temporary) will confirm if that's the cause. Also try reproducing locally on a Windows wheel builder container with `pip wheel --no-binary :all: cryptography` to see native build failure.

jonathan: If pin works, revert the lockfile commit and reopen a regen PR with platform-aware constraints. Reverting the lock is faster to get main green.

marta: Ok I'm going to rerun the failing job to double-check (in case it was flaky). If it fails consistently I'll open a revert PR for the lock regen and include the failing job link.

ci-bot: Rerun started: Build #218 queued for windows-latest.

emily: If rerun is red, I'll start a quick git-bisect on the lockfile commits and report back the first bad commit. Ping me with the commit range (good/bad).

marta: Thanks — will update here. For visibility, pinging @release and @eng-sre if main stays red after 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
